cases.original_concern: Proof 1.2 says the classes are rationally independent because 'a rational relation clears denominators to the excluded nonzero signed integer relation.' Clearing denominators initially gives an integer combination that is torsion modulo the filtration, rather than necessarily zero there. One must also multiply by its finite order before applying the excluded-integer-relation argument. The smooth supplier thm-smooth-winding-zero-iterates-have-infinite-rank-in-every-quotient explicitly includes this torsion-clearing step in Proof 2.1–3.1. The same short justification applies to the TOP argument here.
cases.reason: The proof first excludes every nonzero integer coefficient vector modulo F_{n+1}^{top}, with coefficients unbounded in magnitude. This is an injection Z^{m+1} into the abelian quotient. Rational localization preserves that injection: a rational relation yields, after clearing coefficient denominators, a torsion integer combination; multiplying by its finite order gives a nonzero integer coefficient vector in F_{n+1}^{top}, already excluded. Thus no extra obstruction hypothesis or mathematical prerequisite is missing. The sentence compresses this standard localization algebra; spelling out the torsion step, as the smooth supplier does in 2.1–3.1, would aid a reader but is optional clarification rather than an actual soundness defect.
